note: Curated by research sessions. Development results only; never live interim results. See README.md.

funnel.label: Ideas
funnel.help: Every distinct hypothesis written down in the idea rounds. Cheap to add, most will never be tested.

funnel.label: Designed
funnel.help: Ideas turned into a written, falsifiable test plan with thresholds fixed before any result is looked at.

funnel.label: Screened
funnel.help: Run on historical data. Most results are 'not detected' (too small to see) or 'not testable' (not enough data).

funnel.label: Replicated
funnel.help: The effect held again on separate, untouched historical markets with the definitions frozen.

funnel.label: Live test
funnel.help: Predictions are written down in advance on live data and scored once after a fixed end date.

funnel.label: Cost check
funnel.help: Does the effect survive realistic fees and the spread? Many real effects fail here.

funnel.label: Confirmed edge
funnel.help: Passed a live test and the cost check. Nothing is here yet, and the page says so honestly.

experiments.title: Kalshi lead (live test)
experiments.plain: Does a quick move in a matching Kalshi market show up in Polymarket's price over the next 20 minutes? A frozen model makes the predictions in advance and is scored once, after the end date. We only count rows until then.

experiments.title: Kalshi changes plus gap (live test)

experiments.title: Surprise-move detector (live test)

experiments.title: Order flow continuation
experiments.plain: When trades in a market lean one way for an hour, the price keeps drifting that way. The effect is real in a one-off prospective test, but tiny.

effect.label: +0.36c

experiments.next: None: too small to cover trading costs

experiments.title: Reversal after a price jump

ml.status_note: The main development run (MC1) is parked as a backup: it ran out of memory on the current server. The results below come from earlier development runs on historical data.
learned: Most of the lift over a plain baseline comes from predicting whether a market will move at all (volatility), not which way it will move.
Trading-flow features add a small but stable amount of forecasting value at 2 and 6 hours; wallet-based features add nothing demonstrable.
Order-book features are descriptive only: no demonstrated gain, and they cover just 12.7% of rows.
Three flow interactions (flow x volatility, flow x spread, 1-day change x liquidity) held on fresh markets, but the gross gain is about 1c a trade against about 3.5c of costs.
Forecasting is better in the last 24 hours before a market closes than more than 30 days before, and that held on fresh markets; it rests on an end date read after the fact.

ml.feature_weights_note: These are family-level drop-one ablation deltas (how much log loss gets worse without the family), not SHAP. No per-feature SHAP or importance numbers exist in the committed docs or host outputs yet; the SHAP design is in MULTI_SIGNAL_PIPELINE_DESIGN.md and has not run.
